books.section: Topic 2.5 Interactions Between American Indians and Europeans

options.text: Tobacco profits gave the English reason to keep supplying and settling Virginia

options.misconception: The fighting continued for a decade, and a second great war broke out in 1644.
options.text: The Powhatan stopped fighting after 1622 and made a lasting peace

options.misconception: No peace followed the 1622 attack; the English answered with years of war.
options.text: The English immediately made peace with Opechancanough

options.misconception: Jamestown was never abandoned; the settlers stayed and rebuilt on the same site.
options.text: Jamestown was abandoned and the settlers moved to a safer site

rationales.A: By 1622 tobacco was making Virginia pay: John Rolfe's crop turned a struggling outpost into a profitable colony, and profit kept ships, settlers, and supplies coming even after disaster. A colony that loses money gets abandoned; a colony that makes money gets rebuilt. The 1622 attack was devastating, but it struck a colony that had already found an economic reason to stay.
rationales.B: The fighting continued for a decade, and a second great war broke out in 1644.
rationales.C: No peace followed the 1622 attack; the English answered with years of war.
rationales.D: Jamestown was never abandoned; the settlers stayed and rebuilt on the same site.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what the passage does not say. It never mentions why the English kept coming back after the attack.
2. Look for the colony's reason to live. Background: John Rolfe's tobacco, grown from about 1612, made Virginia profitable.
3. Connect profit to survival. A colony that pays its way gets rebuilt; one that does not gets abandoned.
Remember: when a colony survives a disaster, ask what made it worth saving.

stem: The 1622 attack killed about a quarter of Jamestown's settlers, yet the colony survived and grew. Which of the following best explains why the attack did not destroy the colony?

stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question, summarizing standard background on Jamestown and the Powhatan.
stimulus.text: Jamestown survived its first years only because Powhatan's peoples traded corn to the settlers. But the English kept demanding more food and more land, and within a few years they were raiding Native villages for corn. In 1622, Powhatan's successor Opechancanough struck back, killing 347 settlers — about a quarter of the colony. The English answered with a decade of war, and in 1623 they lured some 200 Powhatan leaders to a peace parley and poisoned their wine. A second great war in 1644 ended with the Powhatan peoples broken and confined to small reserves.
